name: Export control driven GPU price distortion - H20/H200/H800 as worked example
publisher: Reuters / derived from multiple repo records
notes: DERIVED ANALYSIS from existing repo records (acc-fill-cnbc-h800-export-ban, acc-fill-reuters-h800-export-china, acc-fill-dcd-h800-interconnect-halved, used-h800-80gb-market). The US export control regime on advanced GPUs to China has created a two-tier price market. The H800 (H100 with halved interconnect) was created specifically to comply with export controls while still being sellable to China. The H20 (further reduced) is the current generation of China-specific GPUs. Price distortion effects visible in the repo: (1) Used H800 80GB asking $33,900-$41,221 (n=2, small sample) - this is BELOW the used H100 80GB PCIe asking median of $43,000, reflecting the H800's reduced interconnect performance. (2) The H20/H200/H800 are export-controlled variants that trade at a discount to their full-performance equivalents. (3) The export control regime creates a compliance cost that is passed through to buyers. (4) The price distortion is most visible in the used market, where export-controlled variants trade at a 15-25% discount to full-performance equivalents. This is a structural feature of the GPU market that affects deployment cost calculations: an H800 is cheaper than an H100 but also has halved interconnect bandwidth, making it less suitable for multi-GPU inference where interconnect bandwidth matters.
